# gcs-server-extended versus upstream fake-gcs-server

LocalCloud's **gcs-server-extended** builds on **fsouza/fake-gcs-server**. It adds
HTTP authorization integration, HMAC credentials and signature verification,
project-aware bucket listing, same-bucket object moves, and notification recovery.
These additions let local tests exercise permission failures, credential state,
project isolation in listings, and delivery recovery alongside ordinary storage
operations. Upstream supplies the shared storage emulator foundation.

## Scope and evidence

This compares this repository with the community-maintained
[`fsouza/fake-gcs-server`](https://github.com/fsouza/fake-gcs-server), sometimes
referred to as “fake-gcs-storage.” It does not compare against a separate Google
product or claim complete compatibility with production Google Cloud Storage.

Source snapshot reviewed on **2026-10-20**:

- Fork: [`db752a269fdd225771880582af244a1a330b71fd`](https://github.com/LocalGCloud/gcs-server-extended/tree/db752a269fdd225771880582af244a1a330b71fd).
- Upstream: [`3c29d20789f6475f65d2554ad6898c4afd7124bb`](https://github.com/fsouza/fake-gcs-server/tree/3c29d20789f6475f65d2554ad6898c4afd7124bb), resolved from upstream `main` during review.
- The local upstream reference was `b03af29928bed805a8ae65bee02a5c2c5b9b91f5`.
  The [13 intervening upstream commits](https://github.com/fsouza/fake-gcs-server/compare/b03af29928bed805a8ae65bee02a5c2c5b9b91f5...3c29d20789f6475f65d2554ad6898c4afd7124bb)
  change dependencies and CI configuration, with no emulator source changes.
  This permits source-level feature comparison against the local reference;
  dependency changes can still affect runtime behavior.

**Legend:** ✓ = implemented for the behavior named in that row; ✗ = absent for
that behavior in the inspected source; ◐ = a subset, simplified behavior, or a
configuration-dependent limitation explained in the row. A checkmark is a
source-support claim, not a cloud parity certification. Tests linked below are
regression evidence; their presence alone does not mean they were run during
every review. Source-only signing branches are identified explicitly.

The detailed inventory covers exposed HTTP operations, implemented legacy gRPC
methods, client-visible storage behavior, server configuration, and fork
extensions. Internal helpers, language examples, and aliases for the same
operation are not counted as extra features. Headings group rows for navigation;
each row still describes one independently identifiable capability.

## Side-by-side features

| Area | Upstream fake-gcs-server | LocalCloud gcs-server-extended | Value for local testing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Storage basics | Bucket/object APIs, uploads, downloads, copy, compose | Inherits these capabilities | Existing storage tests keep their foundation |
| Authorization | No LocalCloud decision callback | Optional HTTP permission callback; denies when unavailable | Exercise denied reads, writes, and overwrites |
| HMAC credentials | No key-management API | Create, list, read, update, delete; encrypted filesystem registry | Exercise key lifecycle locally |
| Signed requests | Signed URL routing without verification | Verifies supported HMAC XML requests; RSA remains unverified | Reject invalid signatures and expired HMAC URLs |
| Project ownership | Bucket listing does not filter by recorded owner | Records JSON bucket-create project and filters listings | Test multiple project inventories |
| Object moves | Copy/rewrite available; no `moveTo` operation | Same-bucket `moveTo`, source/destination conditions, events | Test staging-to-final object moves |
| Notifications | Configuration API and Pub/Sub publishing | Adds persisted configuration, pending queue, retry, restart replay | Test delivery through temporary Pub/Sub outages |
| CLI wire behavior | Delete operations exist | Corrects successful object/bucket deletes to empty HTTP 204 | Match clients expecting no-content responses |
| HTTP + HTTPS | Both listeners supported | Adds matching of the same public hostname across ports in dual mode; alias/case tests currently fail | Use one exact public hostname across mapped ports |
| Legacy gRPC | Selected Storage v1 methods | Same selected methods; HTTP additions do not extend gRPC | Keep transport expectations explicit |

## Individual-feature matrix

The evidence keys link to the [source and test index](#source-and-test-index),
which provides pinned upstream and fork source links. Shared functionality is
credited to both projects. For a fork-only route, upstream absence is established
from its route registration; for behavioral extensions, inspect the corresponding
upstream implementation as well as the fork implementation.

## Limitations that affect interpretation

- **Authorization is optional and HTTP-only.** With no callback configured,
  ordinary HTTP requests retain open access. The callback evaluates permissions;
  this server does not supply a complete IAM policy engine. Health checks,
  ownership inventory, and the outer batch route bypass callback evaluation;
  batch parts go through middleware. Direct Go/backend calls and gRPC bypass it.
- **Ownership is narrower than a project model.** JSON bucket creation records
  `?project=`. Seeded, auto-created, and gRPC-created buckets can be unattributed
  and are excluded from project-filtered listings. Ownership persistence ignores
  I/O errors. Bucket response `projectNumber` is still the placeholder `"0"`.
- **HMAC is emulator credential handling.** Signing applies to supported XML
  routes, not JSON API HMAC authentication. RSA verification is absent. AWS
  signature recognition does not imply the full S3 API. The encryption root key
  lives beside the encrypted registry; encryption does not protect against a
  reader with access to both files. Positive signing branches need dedicated
  regression/runtime qualification before claiming end-to-end coverage.
- **Notification durability has a defined boundary.** Persisted registry events
  retry and replay, but object writes and outbox writes are separate. A crash
  before queue persistence can lose an event; persistence failure is logged,
  and retry after a publish/ack crash can duplicate delivery. This is not
  transactional exactly-once delivery. The legacy CLI `EventOptions` publisher
  remains a separate path without the registry's durable queue.
- **Moves are same-bucket operations.** They preserve metadata and check source
  and destination conditions; they do not implement hierarchical namespace.
  Filesystem content and metadata changes are not one crash-atomic transaction.
- **Published-port host matching is partial.** Dual mode strips ports and
  compares hostname strings. It does not normalize hostname case or treat
  `localhost`, IPv4 loopback, and IPv6 loopback as interchangeable. The existing
  `TestPublicHostMatchingPublishedPorts` expects those behaviors and fails.
- **Inherited simplifications remain.** Filesystem versioning is unsupported;
  object metageneration remains fixed at 1; bucket metadata includes placeholders;
  ACL storage is not equivalent to permission enforcement; legacy gRPC exposes
  only selected methods and fields. Bucket lifecycle, full bucket IAM policy
  APIs, managed folders, soft-delete restore, and production GCS guarantees are
  outside the implemented route inventory and are not implied by checkmarks.
- **Source versus distribution.** The matrix describes pinned repository code.
  Upstream image/package examples do not distribute these extensions. A local
  test pass does not establish a published image, deployed LocalCloud behavior,
  all SDK compatibility, or a production-cloud comparison.

### Validation during this reconciliation

The prescribed `go test -race -vet all -mod readonly ./...` suite was run using
Go 1.27.1 with stale `GOROOT`/`GOTOOLDIR` overrides removed. The backend,
checksum, config, gRPC, notification, and URL-helper packages passed. The
`fakestorage` package failed `TestPublicHostMatchingPublishedPorts` on five
loopback-alias/hostname-case assertions. This document therefore marks S29
partial; the comparison change does not modify runtime code. Matrix counts,
unique row IDs, evidence references, local source paths, relative document
links, and diff whitespace were checked separately.
